n denotes the number of set elements.
If $(k,m)\in X\times Y$ then $k\in X$, $m\in Y$. $(k,m)\in X\times Y\Rightarrow k\in X,\ m\in Y$

$X\times X$ is written $X^2$ and read 'X two'.
The representation of the cartesian product:
If n(X) = 3, then n(X × X) = 3 × 3 = 9. $n(X)=3 \Rightarrow n(X\times X)=3\times 3=9$
The cartesiem product of the infinite sets and its graphical representation:
First: To represent the cartesian product of $N \times N = \{(x, y) : x \in N, y \in N\}$
Step 1: Draw two perpendicular straight lines, one horizontal (xx') and the other vertical (yy'), intersecting at point O.
Step 2: Represent the natural numbers N on each of the horizontal and vertical lines, starting with the origin O which represents zero.
Step 3: Draw vertical and horizontal lines from the points representing the natural numbers; the points of intersection form the perpendicular graphical net of the cartesian product N × N.
Each point of this net represents one of the ordered pairs in the cartesian product N × N.
For Example: point A represents the ordered pair (3, 2) and point B represents (0, 4).
Second: To represent the cartesien product of $Z \times Z = \{(x, y): x \in Z, y \in Z\}$.
Represent the set of integers on each of the horizontal and vertical lines, where the point O represents the ordered pair (0, 0).
Each point of the net represents one of the pairs in the cartesian product Z × Z.
This net is known as the coordinate plane of Z × Z.
Third: To represent the cartesian product $Q \times Q = \{(x, y) : x \in Q, y \in Q\}$
Fourth: Representing the cartesian product $R \times R = \{(x, y) : x \in R, y \in R\}$
The set of real numbers can be represented on each of the two horizontal and vertical straight lines, and point O represents the ordered pair (o , o).
The horizontal straight line xx' is called the x-axis.
The vertical straight line yy' is called the y-axis.

worked_examples.question: If $X=\{1,2\}$, $Y\{3,4,5\}$ Find: $X\times Y$, and represent it: (First) by the arrow diagram. (Second) by the cartesian diagram.

steps.text: The cartesian product of X × Y is represented by an arrow diagram, or a graphical net, as follows:
First: An arrow diagram. Draw an arrow from each element that represents the first projection (the elements of set X) to each element that represents the second projection (the elements of set Y).
i.e: the arrow diagram of the cartesian product represents each ordered pair by an arrow that starts from its first projection and ends at the second projection.

Second: Cartesian diagram (the perpendicular graphical net). On a perpendicular graph net, the elements of set X are represented horizontally and the elements of set Y vertically. The intersection points of the horizontal and vertical lines represent the ordered pairs of the elements of the cartesian product X × Y.

blocks.text: Relations
A relation of set of X to the set of Y. A relation from a set on it self.
Key term: Relation

In the festival "Reading for All", five students represent the set of X = {a, b, c, d, e} went to the school library to read some books which are represented by the set Y = [science, literature, culture and history]. Student A read a book in science and a book in culture, student b read a book in histroy, student c read a literary book, pupil e read a book of the historical books, but student d didn't read any of these books.

Notice that: The expression "read" connects some of the elements of the set X with the elements of set Y, and it determines a relation between X and Y which is denoted by the symbol R. This relation can be represented by an arrow diagram - as shown in the opposite figure, where we draw an arrow beginning from the student and ending at the type of books he reads.

We can also express the relation from X to Y by the net of the following ordered pairs: {(a, Science), (a, Culture), (b, Histrory), (c, Literature), (e, History)}. This set of ordered pairs are called the relation R.
From the previous, we deduce that
A relation from X to Y, where X, Y are two non-empty sets, connects some or all of the elements of X with some or all of the elements of Y.
X × Y is the set of ordered pairs where the first projection in each ordered pair belongs to X and the second projection belongs to Y. $X\times Y$
If R is a relation from X to Y, then R is a subset of X × Y. $R\subset X\times Y$
The relation from a set to itself
If R is a relation from a set X to X (itself), then R is called a relation on X, and R ⊂ X × X. $R\subset X\times X$

blocks.text: Functions (Mapping)
What you'll learn: Concept of the function; Symbolical expression of the function.
Key term: Functions
Key term: Domain
Key term: Codomain
Key term: Range
The following figures represent three relations from X to Y.
A relation from X to Y is said to be a function if each of the elements of X appears only once as a first projection in one of the ordered pairs of the relation.
The Symbolic representation of the function:

The function is denoted by one of the symbols f or m or Q, etc. The function f from the set X to the set Y is written mathematically as f : X → Y and is read as "f is a function from X to Y". $f : X \rightarrow Y$
If f is a function from X to itself, we say that f is a function on X.

If the ordered pair (x, y) belongs to the function, then the element y is called the image of the element x by the function f, and we express it in one of two forms: f : x ↦ y, read as "the function f maps x to y"; or f(x) = y, read as "f is a function where f(x) = y". $f : x \mapsto y$, $f(x) = y$
The Domain, the codomain and the range
If f is a function from X to Y, i.e. $f: X \to Y$, then
The set X is called the domain of the function f.
The set Y is called the codomain of the function f.
The set of images of the elements of the domain X by the function f is called the range of the function.

1. The domain of the function f is the set $X=\{-1,2,3\}$. 2. The codomain of the function f is the set $Y=\{2,3,5,7\}$. 3. The range of the function f is the set of the images of the elements of X by f and equal to $\{3,5,7\}$.
The range is a subset of the codomain of the function.

blocks.text: Polynomial functions (Lesson 1-4)
The linear function and its graphical representation.
Key term: Polynomial function
Key term: Linear function
Key term: quadratic Function
Key term: The graphical representation of function

The function f: R → R where f(x) = a_0 + a_1 x + a_2 x^2 + ... + a_n x^n, where a_0, a_1, a_2, ... a_n ∈ R, n ∈ N, a_n ≠ 0, is called a polynomial of degree n. $f(x)=a_0+a_1x+a_2x^2+\dots+a_nx^n,\ a_0,a_1,\dots,a_n\in\mathbb{R},\ n\in\mathbb{N},\ a_n\neq 0$
The degree of the polynomial is the highest power of the variable in the function rule.
Linear function
The function f: R → R where f(x) = ax + b, a, b ∈ R, a ≠ 0, is called a linear function or a function of the first degree. $f(x)=ax+b,\ a,b\in\mathbb{R},\ a\neq 0$
The graphical representation of the linear fuction:
Remarks:
It is enough to find two ordered pairs belonging to the function; it is preferred to find a third ordered pair to check the graph.
If f: R → R, f(x) = ax, where a ≠ 0, then it is represented graphically by a straight line passing through the origin (0, 0). $f(x)=ax,\ a\neq 0$
If f: R → R, f(x) = b where b ∈ R, then f is called a constant function. For example f(x) = 3, written as y = 3. It is represented by a straight line parallel to the x-axis. $f(x)=b,\ b\in R$
Values of the constant function f(x) = 3 for x = -1, 1, 2 x, -1, 1, 2 / y = f(x), 3, 3, 3
The quadratic function
The function f: R → R where f(x) = ax² + bx + c, with a, b, c real numbers and a ≠ 0, is called a quadratic function and it is a function of second degree. $f(x)=ax^2+bx+c,\ a\neq 0$
The graphical representation of the quadratic function.
Table of values of f(x)=x² for x from 3 down to -3 x, 3, 2, 1, 0, -1, -2, -3 / y = f(x), 9, 4, 1, 0, 1, 4, 9
The curve of the function f is symmetrical about the y-axis and the equation of the symmetrical axis is x = 0. $x=0$
The coordinate of the vertex of the curve is (0, 0), and the minimum value of the function = 0. $(0,0)$
Generylly:
The function $f(x)=ax^2+bx+c$, where a, b, c are real numbers, $a\neq 0$ has the following properties:
The coordinates of the vertex of the curve are (-b/2a, f(-b/2a)). $\left(\frac{-b}{2a}, f\left(\frac{-b}{2a}\right)\right)$
The curve is open upwards when the coefficient of x² is positive (a > 0), and in this case the function has a minimum value equal to f(-b/2a). $f\left(\frac{-b}{2a}\right)$
The curve is open downward when the coefficient of x² is negative (a < 0), and in this case the function has a maximum value equal to f(-b/2a). $f\left(\frac{-b}{2a}\right)$
The curve is symmetric about the vertical line through the vertex of the curve, whose equation is X = -b/2a; this line is called the axis of symmetry of the function. $x=\frac{-b}{2a}$
